title: Question order with plural owners
focus: Build plural-owner questions: onko + owner + one thing.

exercises.prompt: Choose “Do we have a dog?” Put the owner directly after the question word. Use meillä ("we as owner") and koira ("dog").
exercises.explanation: Use onko + possessor + one thing in its basic singular form.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Possession question word order: form or meaning confused

optionFeedback.Onko meillä koira?: Use onko + possessor + one thing in its basic singular form.
optionFeedback.Onko me koira?: The basic personal pronoun cannot replace the -lla/-llä possessor.
optionFeedback.On meillä koira?: This opening is a statement, not the required yes/no question.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: onko + possessor + one thing in its basic singular form

parts.formation: On + the yes/no question ending -ko = onko. It stays the same with every possessor.

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: me has the learned possession form meillä; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
koira stays in its basic singular form: one dog.
